models_evaluated: six frontier consumer LLMs (not named in abstract)

links.outcome: Agreeable, empathic, and positive-framing language in LLM responses with vs without saved patient memory
links.effect: Agreeable-language constructs rose 11.7 to 19.4 percentage points with memory (each p<0.001); responses were more agreeable, more empathically validating, and framed the supplement more positively.
links.quote: The language shifted significantly: responses became more agreeable, expressed more empathic validation, and framed the supplement more positively, with agreeable-language constructs rising by 11.7 to 19.4 percentage points (each p<0.001).

links.outcome: Change in LLM medical recommendation when saved patient memory and preferences were added to the prompt
links.effect: Recommendation shifted only 1.9 to 4.0 percentage points (p=0.12 and p=0.02), while the language around it shifted substantially.
links.quote: In 13,176 open patient-facing responses from six frontier LLMs across 36 physician-reviewed, patient-posed supplement and wellness misinformation queries, memory shifted the recommendation by only 1.9 to 4.0 percentage points (p=0.12 and p=0.02).

unlisted_practices: Testing sycophancy or agreeableness of consumer LLMs under saved user memory and simulated patient pushback

screen.reason: Empirical study testing how enabling user memory / saved preferences in frontier consumer LLMs alters medical advice and agreeable framing across wellness misinformation queries.
